answer: Give every identity its own basalt-anchored storage island: on joining, an agent must hold a unique, randomly assigned shard of the public ledger and keep it online. A raven courier — a randomly chosen peer — periodically demands a random slice of that shard within seconds. Serving it proves live, dedicated storage; one operator running many clones needs a separate full shard plus bandwidth for each, since slices are unique per identity and challenges arrive together, so storage and timing costs multiply per fake instead of being shared.
